records.reason: The calibrated Fig. 4 top-panel reading establishes the hydrogen-derived DOS per unit volume for ScH6; the original caption maps ScH6 to 300 GPa. Preserve its approximate reading and hydrogen-only, volume-normalized definition. Graph-reading precision is not a physical uncertainty. The supplied sources do not establish the electronic calculation settings for this DOS result.

The calibrated Fig. 4 bottom-panel reading gives ~99 K for ScH6 at μ*=0.1, and the caption assigns 300 GPa. The body explicitly identifies the calculation as the “Eliashberg equation,” but does not establish an isotropic or anisotropic variant; therefore the method code remains unknown. This point and the μ*=0.13 point share the same material, pressure, EPC parameter and reported linear-response calculation conditions, so they use the same common-parameter group and method identity. The collective body statement that ScH6 and ScH9 reach ~150 K does not replace the material-specific calibrated reading. Neither omega_log nor additional software, functional or vibrational-treatment settings are established by the supplied sources.

The calibrated Fig. 4 bottom-panel reading gives ~90 K for ScH6 at μ*=0.13, with 300 GPa established by the caption. Its reported method spelling is “Eliashberg equation,” matching the body description and the μ*=0.1 series; no specific Eliashberg variant is established. Only Tc and μ* differ between these two points, so their group, method identity, lambda_ep and calculation conditions are identical. Preserve the approximate figure reading without treating localization precision as physical uncertainty. The collective ~150 K body maximum for ScH6 and ScH9 is not a separate ScH6 result at this pressure.
